This game is so well designed. Every second of every run requires tough, meaningful decisions. Rougelike games are probably my favorite genre, and I think this game should be recognized as one of the best of its kind

Nope, I hated every moment of it, it has the worst approach to roguelike, there's no way to do anything meaningful in your first 10 runs or so, you have to slowly grind out materials to build shit that grants your hero +0.17 attack power and such, it's the clicker approach to game design. the game only really allows for one kind of strategy, and that's to optimize your loops as much as possible, and you might be thinking "well, yeah, that's what makes it fun and challenging!" but in that case I'd rather play a zachtronics game or something, perhaps this is just not for me, I've abandoned it, say it filtered me if you want, but this feels more like a chore than an actual videogame.

Final Score: 3/5 personally, about 3.5/5 unbiased.
Anyone that enjoys card games is going to like this one. It's very addicting and fun. I think I put 33 hours on in within' 2 days? Maybe 3?

It's not bad it's just not rewarding in the way games like this should be.

Fantastic game but just too punishing and that guts it. Progression takes too long, if you kept 50% or more of the loot after a fail instead of 30% maybe it would keep the momentum better so that I'd really want to keep coming back to it. As it is it is addictive and has all the right elements in there but there's this unnecessary mobile gameish wall with bosses. You have to grind to be OP. Otherwise you throw most of your progress away and then have to go through the same boring setup for each run, which means you grind a lot of safe boring runs.

I understand that it's a roguelike/-lite but the core loop in this genre should be interesting enough vs the difficulty, and this in this it isn't. At it's core it's an autobattler like all autobattlers should be, and I really mean that as a praise. It just doesn't have to be this boring to grind. If you're still on the fence, I think you may enjoy this if you enjoyed FTL, If you didn't, then probably not.
Excellent Idle Game If you love magic the gathering feeling and Rogue-lite RPG and Comfy Retro Music

Really fun game, it hits that perfect amount of engagement that you can pay attention to something on your second screen like youtube, while enjoying some enjoyable progress in this game. It also has a VERY solid permanent progression system that a lot of roguelikes dont quite get right.
Great game! Really enjoy the look and feel it as well. Really accessible and fun to play, but definitely has enough depth to get lost in it if you want to.

To my shame I never made a positive review of this game when I played it.

I just never finished it on PC. On the mobile however, I lost hours and hours fully completing it.

It's my opinion that it is much better enjoyed on it's very good mobile port and I would encourage others who bounced off this game like I did to do the same.

At first glance I passed right by this game, it kept creeping its way into my suggestions and I gave it a shot. Then I quickly lost 60 hours of my life playing it. The game is like visual cocaine, its constantly making you come back for more. It feels good to find a new combo in your card placement or to stomp a boss that previously beat you down like it was nothing.

If anything about this game looks appealing to you just go ahead and get it, it will be worth it.

As the game's name stated, it's all about loops. In this case, the loops are not fun enough to be repeated for too many times. The gameplay was stagnant (new elements are coming very slowly), grindy (farming for materials that are based on chance) and finally intolerable (after 21 hours). Graphics and audio aren't the strong suit of this game nor replayability. The loops need to be operated (in not so funny ways) to keep the character improving/surviving so it feels like a chore with little reward (for the player).
As a big rougelike and idle game fan this game feels like it tries to do both and unfortunately fails on both accounts :/

This is the essence of gaming defined by its primordial elements. In 2026, we rarely have this and it''s something to be treasured. Yes, there is a grind here and part of what's to be treasurred is figuring out what the grind IS. This game makes no apologies - not in terms of urgency, time commitment, ark of learning nor any other metric with which you might expect to levy against this irregularity yet it is a testament to what developers can achieve, free from greediness and perpetual revenue.

In short, this game is what we needed - simplicity, reason and punishment, all in one delectable package.

You know that one feeling you get when you have an itch right up your butt hole on like the corner that's a bit hard to scratch, but when you do, it feels amazing. Well loop hero is like that, but a game.
Prepare to die, a lot... But it's like a love-hate relationship, you can't get away cause it's totally addictive. I just love it, or hate it? Nah, just love.

As someone who has played the game multiple times through its a very fun experience but it's very questionable on how much of a rogue like it is. When you go through each run(loop) you have a set of cards you can select. These cards can be placed on the map and change the play-through such as spawning different enemies to buffing your character or enemies. This mechanic is very fun but limited in how much truly different options you get. You also have a camp which unlocks more content and buffs to your character from the loot you complete each loop; an alright mechanic but very typical in a rogue lite fashion.

That said it is a truly gorgeous game with a very well written story. I love the concept of building the map up from nothing and deciding how you want to plan your routes. I really do think this game is either a loved game or a meh game for people. I think for most people if this game goes on sale for 5 to 10 its well worth the money but maybe watch a video of someone doing a play-through on it before deciding. If a developer sees this know I really hope you guys create another game with the same quality of writing and art, you guys have a lot of potential!

This is one of those games where you read the glowing reviews, but based on the description of the gameplay you're thinking "really?"

Then you buy the game and spend 10-20 minutes playing, and your reaction is "this is what they were raving about?"

Then three hours go by and you're thinking, "my first meeting isn't until 1 p.m., so I can probably play another 2-3 hours."

Deceptively simple game loop that is extraordinarily compelling.

Loop Hero is a highly addicting game. After getting it on release, i found myself drawn to this game over and over again, just wanting to do another round to upgrade my camp afterwards and unlock stuff.

The game is a rougelite game, with a card mechanic that lets you place cards on tiles of the map. Some go on the road, some next to the road and some away from the road of your randomly generated loop. The most interesting part is, how those cards influence enemy spawns, your hero´s stats, other effects and even each other. Its a lot of fun to find working setups for clearing the chapter or going for an endless round. Placing/erasing cards, changing equipment and choosing traits on level ups is how the player mostly interacts during a run, while the rest unfolds automatically.

The game has also a camp building/upgrading mechanic between rounds which gives you access to new cards, classes (3 at release), small passive boni and other stuff. The classes are pretty distinct from each other and fun to play around with.
I personally also like the game sprites with its dark aesthetic.
The price is pretty low and i can definitely recommend this game.

Loop Hero is a deck builder. It's also a roguelite. It's a... reverse tower defense strategic builder? Whatever probably correct descriptor you can toss at the game, it's a phenomenal experience. There is a ton of strategy behind the seemingly simple exterior. Place different tiles together for new and different effects. Stack your run with crazy chaining effects that are too good to spoil in a review. Enjoy the fantastic spritework while being serenaded by the great soundtrack.

Loop Hero is an easy recommendation to almost any style of gamer. You can even pause at any time to contemplate your imminent death forever! Most will get 20-40 hours of playtime, but you can find much more if you get addicted to the loops like I have.

This would be neutral if steam had that option, but as a critical review it's probably leaning closer towards negative than positive.

Fun for some few hours, painfully slow and unrewarding afterwards.

Fun: Learning what is and isn't powerful, exploring combinations, unlocking buildings/cards, improving your builds until you can defeat the bosses.

The rest: Really formulaic and requires guides if you want to retain your sanity, i.e. every change in your built would require hours upon hours on fruitless expeditions, just to see if x is viable against y boss, which becomes the only deciding factor, after you know what enemy tiles to place/avoid. Very little built variety, samey weapons, armours, items, perks—there's always something that dwarfs the competition/is objectively superior to all the other options, you would be stupid not to gun for that.

This game would be great if the path you can walk wasn’t so narrow, if there was more than a handful of ways you can become powerful enough to achieve anything. It's really slow-paced on top of that, which results in runs blending together even worse than they would otherwise.

Maybe this will get addressed in future updates, but for now I'm definitely done with it.
Very fun, lot of strategy, bit of min/maxing, many combinations to experiment with. Tough but fair game. Enjoyed every minute of it.

I am surprised by how much I have ended up enjoying this game!! I was not sure if the style was for me, but it the most exciting game I have played in a long time. I would encourage anybody to give it a try.

Fun little time waster. Easy to pick up and put down. You do not control the combat but you set up the conditions of combat. It is fun to experiment with different decks to get a feel for what the cards do. Like most roguelites there is not much explained and several hidden combos to discover. It can seem very difficult until you work out a winning strategy, but once you do you are unstoppable. Grinding and building upgrades are an easy path to winning. My high play time is from leaving the game on pause for a long time. I probably played about 10 hrs or so and completed the first 3 chapters. Did not really feel compelled to take it to the end. The strategy for doing so was obvious but required too much grinding to get resources and build. If you enjoy thinking and planning more than jumping and shooting this would be worth it.

great game, retro games are really rare these days and even tough i'm not that fond of repetitive gameplay, the game is still addictive, choosing between 3 classes with different types of biomes and enemy cards can make you spend a lot of free time.

Overall the game is awesome, for its cost and its repetitiveness it can be a time consumer if you have a steam deck.

Interesting story. Simple machanism.

It is essentially a deck building rogue like game each loop.

Great game, very addictive! My only problem is how grindy the late-game gets - expecting you to grind 20-30 loops for an hour each before progression is even plausible. A bit frustrating, but there is so much experimentation you can do while you do that to keep you engaged you'll end up doing it anyway. It's got that 'one more expedition' feel to it.

The graphics were good for pixels, but the FRPG gameplay was really neat: building base, risking 1/3 of your loot from death, the encylopedia, the variety of build sequence, the 3 classes and many trikets that improved their survival. The best part was the terrain tiles that you place yourself to make a beautiful map at the end of a run. This game comes highly recommended for FRPG, single-player fans that want to recreate on a budget for hours and hours. I ran this game while waiting on CDs in another game and I really like to clicking out of UI minimizes and pauses. A great game to play while at work LOL.
Great game, each time you play you get a little further. It encourages you to come back and try to be just a little better next time.
This game is a fun game to spend time with. So much to explore, builds to try, and to think you don't even really control the hero
Haven't played anything like it really. It's not super engaging or thought provoking but it has good storytelling at least and is a fun way to pass the time until it gets boring.

Well designed Roguelike with a great soundtrack and amazing pixel graphics. The progression is fun to figure out but once you reach a certain point, you become a god of the loop. I definitely hope they make an expansion or a sequel.

played this just under 2 hours and didnt care for any of it. its basically an idle game, something you just let run while doing something else, takes minimal effort and not at all what i was expecting. unless you are looking for a small idle game, this isnt for you and its not at all worth the price they are asking for. get it on sale or not at all IMO

As of right now, there's nothing that makes me want to go back to this game. Take this review with a massive grain of salt, read some other folk's reviews. Unfortunately, the ending feels and just looks incomplete, as if they intended to have more updates in the future, but it seems like the project has been abandoned / finished since 2022. 

Meh. I'd say to pass on it, unfortunately. Also has some weird things happening with the UI when in the base camp, trying to upgrade things.

There's somethin about these mouse only roguelikes like Slay the Spire that have just been so fun lately. The LOOP of my HERO is super addictive and learning elements and interactions between said elements while building strategies through failures is so fun
When back to play this a second time because it's such a casual/strategy game mix that always hits the spot.
The music is punchy, the encounters are fun, and the pace of Loop Hero never feels slow, which is funny for an auto-battler.

Grind Hero - Too much loop!

t starts off quite interesting, but it takes over 30 hours to reach the endgame. And it stays the same throughout. There's no challenge other than mindless grinding.

I put ten hours in and thought I had saw a nice little game. Went to look up some info and possible combo's I missed and realized I'd barely scratched the surface of this game. If you like planning, decision making, and adventure get this game. Love this concept and expect a series of half baked copies coming down the road. This is a FTL, Darkest Dungeon, Slay the Spire level of setting the bar for a genre. I can't explain how blown my mind is right now at the amount of depth I just saw.
Got it for 3 dollars and have passed 17 hours on it so far. Is it fun? Not especially, there's not much player agency or skill to it, is it a nice thing to run next to chat to fill in the time? yeah
When are we getting loop hero dlc or an update, this is like one of my favorite games. The art style alone is peak cinema.

I initially had a positive review but I have had to update it to negative. I hate games with bad math. Monster says it deals 62 damage but I am being hit for 138 damage. That is dumb. There is no way to account for or manage what will happen because the developers were not intelligent enough to give the player accurate information or maliciously wanted to make the game bad. Either way that is a very big negative. Loop Hero could and should be a good game but it would need talented people to work on it. The core concept is nice but the execution is deplorably bad.

good game, spent hours grinding, now I just hope for a Loop Hero 2 that would include maybe more classes but also more gameplay diversity to make it replayable other than creating a new save to optimize more

I love the art style, soundtrack, and the core concept is really unique. The only problem is, for the pricetag, there really isn't enough content. After the first 10 hours, it becomes very easy and repetitive. However I love this game, I just hope there's more planned soon.
This game is definitely unique. It's a roguelike-deckbuilder-map tile manager-game. The best part is definitely the music and art style!

I like roguelike base builder and idle games a lot but that's my first dickbuilder therefore i was expecting something different. The low level manual grinding (replacing armor, planting cards) if not much fun. Therefore no reccomendation for those who don't like active play in a idle game.
This game is awesome, definitely worth a purchase, if you're into procedural rogue-likes at all, i'd recommend giving this game a try!

The game is really stingy with certain resources which just makes it needlessly grindy. Once you've built up your 50th-100th loop you really start to resent the game since you're just going through the motions to get that 1 specific resource you need to unlock the next building.

Exploration + optimization game

I liked the story and I liked the mechanics. The whole loop system is still pretty unique, so you can't just apply knowledge from other games. That's what I want in a roguelite

For the money this is very fun and very replayable AND i love how the active party is placing tiles and sorting loot rather than active combat BECAUSE it's casual, yet there are levels of strategy and deckbuilding and chance that make this truly a engaging rpg.
The only thing i could ask for is more.
